_meta.description: PEER VERDICT (qualitative-only) vs the ~6 closest REAL competitors. Each peer carries a Qual Score /10 and a VERDICT word (CLEAR LEADER/STRONG/SOLID/AVERAGE/WEAK/AVOID). self marks the holding; rank = its position; why = decisive factor; plus best-to-own, peer-to-avoid and an action. Separate axis from the portfolio quality score.
_meta.verdicts: CLEAR LEADER | STRONG | SOLID | AVERAGE | WEAK | AVOID

NH.why: Best low-cost cardiac/oncology delivery and strong India margins (+400 bps YoY in Q1 FY27); behind only Apollo's scale and pharmacy/diagnostics ecosystem. Cayman drives growth; the Nov-2025 UK PPGHL acquisition adds scale but dilutes margins and ROCE near term.

HCG.why: Unmatched dedicated-oncology depth and network, but thin margins, high leverage and ~2.5% ROE place it behind the diversified majors; Q1 FY27 adj. EBITDA +20% and margin guidance of 21-22% in two years are the first signs of an earnings inflection.

ASTERDM.why: Now a top-3 platform by beds with 22% proforma margins and a Kerala/South brand after the Jul-2026 QCIL merger, but lower ROCE (11%), unproven synergies and a PE co-promoter keep it behind Apollo/Max/Narayana until integration delivers.

PARKHOSPS.why: Strong North-India cluster economics (26-27% EBITDA, ~18% ROIC, lowest capex per bed) and 20%+ growth on a now debt-free balance sheet, but small scale, 77% government-payor mix and regional concentration keep it below the national majors.

DATAPATTNS.why: Highest margins (FY26 OPM 40%) and the only fully vertically-integrated (FPGA-to-system) private design house, now a ₹586 Cr radar-electronics supplier to BEL itself (21-Aug-2026); trails only BEL on scale and order-book depth, ahead of Paras/ideaForge on profitability and balance sheet.

ASTRAMICRO.why: Strong RF/microwave franchise with deep DRDO/HAL ties and now the best order cover in years (₹4,300 Cr after the Jul-2026 Uttam radar win), but lumpier quarterly delivery, longer receivables and a lower promoter stake than Data Patterns and BEL.

best_own.name: Bharat Electronics
best_own.why: best mix of scale and returns

MTARTECH.why: Elite micron-tolerance work across nuclear/space/clean-energy with the strongest order-book cover in the set (₹5,143 Cr, ~6x revenue) after Q1 FY27 revenue +130%; still behind Azad on margins and customer diversification, and promoter selling/pledge is a governance drag.

AVANTEL.why: Niche Navy/DRDO satcom and SDR player whose first-ever ₹1,000 Cr order book (Jun-26) and Q1 FY27 rebound (+36% revenue) lift visibility, but FY26 margin collapse, ROE 5% and 627-day cash cycle keep overall quality average versus scaled peers.

CYIENTDLM.why: Cyient pedigree with AS9100/NADCAP aero edge and a record ₹2,598 Cr order book (Q1 FY27 revenue +34%), but ROCE below 10%, heavy working capital and FY26's revenue dip keep it behind Kaynes/Syrma and well behind Data Patterns' margins.

NETWEB.why: Only listed end-to-end AI/HPC OEM with a Class-I procurement moat, 45% ROE and Q1 FY27 revenue +172% — still top of its niche; working-capital build, promoter selling (Feb 2026) and rich valuation are the knocks. Unlisted VVDN swapped for listed Cyient DLM.

best_own.name: Netweb Technologies
best_own.why: unique moat; add on valuation cooling

POWERINDIA.why: Near-exclusive HVDC franchise for India's renewable-grid build-out, fastest order-book growth in the set (backlog ₹32,222 Cr, Q1 FY27 revenue +69%) and 22% ROE at 29% ROCE. Premium valuation the only knock.

best_own.name: ABB India
best_own.why: broader automation mix at high RoCE

HBLENGINE.why: Primary Kavach ATP supplier — first RDSO-approved on Version 4.0 with ₹1,714 Cr CLW and ₹575 Cr ICF orders — and stand-out 45% ROE; Q1 FY27 margin dip shows execution is lumpy and tied to Railway schedules.

SIEMENS.why: Broadest automation + smart-infrastructure + rail franchise with the strongest order momentum (Q1 FY27 orders +43.9% organic, backlog ₹46,670 Cr), but Q1 FY27 operating margin of 7.6% and negative FY26 cash conversion leave it behind ABB India on returns and margin resilience.

THERMAX.why: Broadest energy-and-environment franchise in the set with a record ₹14,045 Cr backlog, but the Q1 FY27 ₹91 Cr legacy-EPC overrun, FEPL/bio-CNG losses and 10.6% ROE keep it behind product-led, cash-rich Cummins and Triveni.

avoid.name: BHEL
avoid.why: weak returns, execution and PSU drag

TRITURBINE.why: Global #2 in sub-100 MW industrial turbines with 34% ROCE, a fast-growing aftermarket and export book, still the best-run name in its niche; the Q1 FY27 margin dip and domestic slowdown narrow the gap to Siemens Energy.

ELGIEQUIP.why: #2 global brand in its set with oil-free/Demand=Match IP, 22% ROCE and now 23% growth across all regions (Q1 FY27); trails only Atlas Copco on scale and margin, ahead of Ingersoll Rand India and Kirloskar on technology and reach.

INOXINDIA.why: Only full-stack Indian cryogenic OEM with 34% ROCE, a record ₹1,686 Cr export-heavy backlog and new aerospace (AS 9100D), semiconductor and fusion credentials; dominates the listed peer set despite weak working-capital conversion.

best_own.name: INOX India
best_own.why: domestic monopoly + high RoCE + space/LNG optionality

NEULANDLAB.why: Rare peptide/GLP-1 plus custom-manufacturing franchise compounding fast (FY26 revenue +37%, Q1 FY27 +119%, ROCE 26.5%); behind Divi's on scale and balance sheet, level with Laurus, ahead of most on growth and margins. Molecule concentration and capex-cycle ROCE dilution are the risks.

SUVEN.why: Rare Indian pure-play CNS NCE developer with a fully enrolled Phase 3 and ₹857 Cr of funding, but no revenue, accelerating burn and binary trial risk place it below cash-generative innovation-led peers.

best_own.name: Sun Pharma
best_own.why: specialty innovation funded by generics cash flows

avoid.name: Sun Pharma Advanced Research (SPARC)
avoid.why: serial trial setbacks, perpetual cash burn

BIOCON.why: Global biosimilar pioneer (insulins, mAbs) now with 100% of Biocon Biologics and improving earnings (Q1 FY27 PAT pre-exceptionals +245%), but weak consolidated ROE, leverage and Syngene drag keep quality below the large generics.

avoid.name: Biocon
avoid.why: leverage + low ROE until biosimilars scale

SHILPAMED.why: Oncology HPAPI IP plus a now-profitable complex-formulations and biologics stack (Q1 FY27 revenue +45%, EBITDA 30%, net debt/EBITDA 1.3x) closes the gap to Natco/Gland, though ROCE (12.5%) still trails Divi's/Laurus.

avoid.name: Natco Pharma
avoid.why: earnings hinge on lumpy US launches post-Revlimid; concentration risk

SANSERA.why: Fastest-growing name in the set (Q1 FY27 revenue +33%, EBITDA 19.2%) with a differentiated aero/defence/semiconductor order book, but still trails Bharat Forge and Sundram Fasteners on scale, returns (ROCE 13.6%) and promoter skin-in-the-game (29% holding).

SONACOMS.why: Best EV-traction-motor exposure and platform-level switching-cost moat, now endorsed by DENSO's 49% JV buy-in, with a record 54% revenue quarter; margins at the low end of guidance and the promoter-trust dispute are the watch-items.

SKFINDIA.why: Top-2 bearing maker with strong after-market and ~29% ROE; Schaeffler edges ahead on breadth and EV-drivetrain content.

KPITTECH.why: Pure-play software-defined-vehicle specialist with deep OEM lock-in and 19 straight growth quarters; recent PAT dip and customer concentration the risks.

AFFLE.why: India's #1 mobile ad-tech with a 3bn-device-profile data moat and conversion-based CPCU model; leads listed India, though global majors out-scale it.

RATEGAIN.why: Largest India-listed travel-tech SaaS, now a top global player after Sojern (14,000+ customers, 320+ data partners) with rate-shopping/intent data network effects and 700+ integrations; leverage and integration keep it just behind IDeaS.

best_own.name: RateGain
best_own.why: only listed-India pure-play with data moat

MAPMYINDIA.why: Only profitable Indian maps + location platform with a 30-year sovereign-data moat, 40% EBITDA margin and 12% ROE; dominant among listed Indian peers and winning enterprise accounts from Google (Amazon Now), but faces Google on the consumer side.

TATACOMM.why: Owns a global submarine-cable backbone with an enterprise/NaaS moat now benefiting from data-centre interconnect demand; 2.1x leverage, a loss-making digital portfolio and slower underlying growth keep it behind Airtel on overall quality.

INDUSTOWER.why: Largest Indian towerco with 18.6% ROE, ~267,600 towers and the dividend restored (₹14/share, Apr-26) after the Vi receivable clean-up; flat rentals and Vi funding remain the swing factors on quality.

best_own.name: Indus Towers
best_own.why: scale + ROE + reinstated ~4% dividend yield; Vi recovery optionality

RAILTEL.why: Exclusive rail-track fibre, a ₹11,747 Cr order book and a data-centre push on a zero-debt, 23% ROCE balance sheet; PSU execution pace, 175-day government receivables and 4-5% project margins cap the re-rating.

GMRAIRPORT.why: Operates Delhi + Hyderabad 60-year concessions plus Goa, Nagpur and the new Bhogapuram — natural monopolies now profitable (FY26 PAT ₹472 Cr) with non-aero >50% of revenue; high infrastructure leverage and AERA regulation are the knocks.

CARBORUNIV.why: Full-stack abrasives-to-electrominerals (SiC) franchise with Murugappa backing, but FY26 ROCE of 11% and ₹135 Cr overseas write-downs leave Grindwell Norton (ROCE ~21%, Q1 FY27 PAT +22%) ahead on returns; Q1 FY27 standalone rebound and raised FY27 guidance (10 Aug 2026) support HOLD.

best_own.name: Grindwell Norton
best_own.why: higher RoCE, cleaner returns, no overseas drag

GRINDWELL.why: Saint-Gobain technology, 21% ROCE, net-cash balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation; leads listed-India abrasives on returns and consistency — Q1 FY27 PAT +22% with 19.6% OPM versus CUMI's 9% OPM and overseas write-downs.

SYRMA.why: Design-led EMS with RFID, MedTech and defence niches and the fastest growth in the set (Q1 FY27 revenue +68%, PAT +112%), but smaller scale and thinner margins (~10-11%) than Dixon/Kaynes.

avoid.name: PG Electroplast
avoid.why: capital-intensive, RAC-seasonal EMS with lower margins and a FY26 guidance cut (Sep-2025)

AVALON.why: US-export box-build EMS with a clean-energy/industrial/rail niche now growing ~50% with 12% EBITDA margin, 23% ROCE and a Zollner JV; still smaller and more working-capital-heavy than Dixon/Kaynes, with a loss-making US arm.

TVSELECT.why: TVS-brand POS servicing niche but commoditised peripherals, very low ROE (1.7%) and a renewed Q1 FY27 loss; smallest and least profitable of the set.

DLINKINDIA.why: Established SMB networking brand with ROCE 26%, debt-free balance sheet and Q1 FY27 revenue +30.5%, but shallow distribution-led moat and 8% OPM versus Cisco/Aruba's enterprise franchises.

MOSCHIP.why: Pioneering Indian fabless ASIC designer with semiconductor-mission tailwinds, but tiny scale, lumpy milestone revenue (Q1 FY27 PAT -78%), a declining promoter stake and promoter-linked Supreme Court litigation that has stalled its Vayavya acquisition; far below Tata Elxsi/LTTS on margins and governance depth.

SASKEN.why: Deep chipset/modem software ties and a broadened Borqs/Silicon platform now growing 24% organically, but 9.5% EBITDA, 7% ROE, 56% top-5 concentration and negative cash flow keep it well below Tata Elxsi/KPIT/LTTS.

RAMCOSYS.why: Sticky aviation-MRO ERP niche and an FY26 return to profit (OPM 23%), but years of slow growth, Q1 FY27 margin slippage and inconsistent profitability keep it below the product leaders.

RPTECH.why: #2 national IT distributor with NVIDIA/AMD lines and 60%+ growth, but thin distribution margins vs Redington's scale/cloud mix and a new governance question mark after the Aug-2026 ID resignation.

REDINGTON.why: Largest, most-diversified IT distributor with a cloud/AI-solutions mix, 22% ROCE and record Q1 FY27 profit; leads the set by a wide margin despite thin margins and the Arena drag.

FRACTAL.why: AI-native Fortune-500 analytics with Qure.ai optionality and improving margins (Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA 16.8%); leads India peers on scale (FY26 revenue ₹3,300 Cr) and client depth, behind global Palantir on platform economics.

LATENTVIEW.why: Profitable pure-play analytics with strong cash, but US-tech client concentration has cut FY27 growth guidance to ~12% (03-Aug-2026), ROE is ~12% and a new CEO (15-Jul-2026) must deliver an M&A-led USD 200 Mn FY28 target.

PROTEAN.why: PAN/NPS monopoly-like franchise with widening DPI mandates, but far lower and more volatile margins (Q1 FY27 EBITDA 10%) and slower earnings growth than CAMS/CDSL/KFin.

URBANCO.why: Full-stack home-services leader with an accelerating, now-profitable core (Q1 FY27 revenue +44%, core margin 6.9%), but a fragmented market, InstaHelp losses and volatile consolidated margins keep it below platform leaders.

UNIECOM.why: Profitable, net-cash SaaS with marketplace integrations and network effects in enterprise OMS/WMS, but SMB churn, price competition and a sub-scale Shipway; margins dipped in Q1 FY27 on growth investments.

NIITLTD.why: 30-year brand and corporate-skilling shift but very low ROE and high PE post Coforge split.

NEPHROPLUS.why: Asia's largest dialysis chain with chronic-patient stickiness, a PPP model and a now net-cash balance sheet delivering 24% growth at 23% margins, but ROE below 10%, government receivables and early-stage international bets keep it behind the global majors.

INDGN.why: Niche life-sciences digital/commercial-ops player with top-pharma stickiness and 40% revenue growth (Q1 FY27), but client concentration and a margin dip to 16.9% during its GenAI investment phase.

YATHARTH.why: Fast-growing NCR multi-specialty (Q1 FY27 revenue +52%, ARPOB ₹34,758) with improving occupancy and a proven acquisition playbook, but small scale, 23% margins diluted by new units, rising debt and promoter selling.

VIYASH.why: Fully backward-integrated API + formulation platform delivering fast margin repair (Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 21.6%) and near-zero net debt, but a short combined-entity record and a PE promoter that began selling (10.88% on 26 Aug 2026) keep it mid-table.

WOCKPHARMA.why: Zaynich's US FDA approval (30 May 2026) and four profitable quarters lift Wockhardt from turnaround to option-rich small pharma, but with ROE 6%, ₹2,233 Cr gross debt and the US launch still ahead, quality trails the large-cap peers.

avoid.name: Wockhardt
avoid.why: await US commercial traction; ROE 6%, P/E ~80x

GAUDIUMIVF.why: High-margin, scalable IVF network with a trust/referral moat, but Q1 FY27 (14 Aug 2026) exposed doctor/centre dependence — growth 9%, EBITDA margin 12.5% — and FY26 receivables of 187 days weaken earnings quality versus larger private peers.

ENTERO.why: Only listed pure-play B2B pharma-distribution consolidator with route density and improving margins (5.0% EBITDA, ROCE 21% in Q1 FY27); still thin-margin and WC-heavy versus Apollo's integrated pharmacy franchise.

best_own.name: Apollo Pharmacy
best_own.why: integrated retail + hospital ecosystem, superior returns

LAXMIDENTL.why: India's largest integrated dental-products maker with aligner/scanner optionality and record Q1 FY27 (₹74.7 Cr, 19.2% margin), but still small (FY26 revenue ₹278 Cr) vs global majors.

RUBICON.why: Complex drug-delivery formulator with 27% ROE, 36% ROIC and 50%+ growth, now raising margin guidance; behind Divi's/Laurus on scale and diversification, with US concentration and PE-promoter selling as the offsets.

BLUEJET.why: One of few global contrast-media intermediate makers with 53-56% gross margins, debt-free and QIP-funded for Vizag, but FY26 PI/API destocking (-35%) exposed customer concentration; unlisted Bracco swapped for listed CDMO peer Neuland.

FREDUN.why: Fastest top-line grower in the set (FY26 +40%, Q1 FY27 +90%) with a differentiated pet-care leg, but sub-scale, leveraged and now carrying a use-of-proceeds governance question; Caplin's cash-rich LatAm model remains the quality benchmark.

best_own.name: Caplin Point
best_own.why: high-ROCE, net-cash LatAm branded generics + injectables

avoid.name: Jagsonpal Pharma
avoid.why: sub-scale domestic branded generics with slow growth

ANURAS.why: Long-term contracted custom-synthesis order book and new US/formulations platforms, but high debt (₹1,867 Cr), promoter pledges, working-capital intensity and margin pressure vs leaders.

STALLION.why: Largest refrigerant-gas importer/distributor now building R32/HFO capacity, but low-margin distribution, price/regulatory risk and a promoter stake that slipped to 47.8% keep it below the integrated fluorochemical producers.

GULFOILLUB.why: Top-3 lubricant brand with 24% ROE, 72% payout and the fastest volume growth in the set (Q1 FY27 +17% vs industry 3-4%) after converting the 2026 supply crisis into share; still behind Castrol on brand pull and carries the EV overhang and crude-linked margins.

ASALCBR.why: Integrated ENA+IMFL+bottling with steady returns but small scale and state-policy exposure.

TRIVENI.why: Integrated sugar-distillery-water group with AA+ balance sheet and a completed value-unlocking demerger, but regulated sugar economics, 9% ROCE and ethanol policy risk keep it below Balrampur/EID Parry.

GREAVESCOT.why: #1 3-wheeler engine franchise plus a scaling Ampere EV arm (Q1 FY27 revenue +31%), but EV losses, a 5.8% consolidated EBITDA margin and parent-funded subsidiary capital keep overall quality below Cummins/Kirloskar.

VSTTILLERS.why: Dominant power-tiller niche (>70% share) with Mitsubishi-derived technology, a debt-free AA- balance sheet and a record FY26, but small-tractor competition, subsidy/monsoon cyclicality and a 10% ROE keep it mid-table.

ECOSMOBLTY.why: Asset-light B2B employee-transport leader with 28% ROCE and strong volume growth, but a fragmented, price-competitive market has pushed margins to ~10% (FY27 guide cut Aug-2026).

LANDMARK.why: Largest premium multi-brand dealer with a high-margin after-sales annuity and a profit recovery under way (Q1 FY27 PAT ~2x), but OEM agency-model shift, leverage and cyclicality persist.

MENONBE.why: Dominant bimetal engine-bearing niche with 22% ROE, 25.5% ROCE, dividends and re-accelerating growth (Q1 FY27 +36.6%), now diversifying into brakes/railways and US exports; ICE-EV risk, tractor cyclicality and Aug-2026 promoter selling cap the score.

ARE&M.why: #2 lead-acid maker with strong cash generation and a Li-ion gigafactory/BESS push, but FY26 margin (10.8%) and Q1 FY27 (9.6%) missed the 13% target and New Energy remains loss-making; lead-acid maturity and cell-execution risk keep it SOLID rather than STRONG.

RIR.why: Niche rectifiers/thyristors for heavy industry with a bold SiC pivot; Q1 FY27 growth (+29%) and NSE listing help, but very small scale, negative FY26 cash flow, ₹618 Cr capex burden and a 176x P/E keep it at the bottom of the set.

SCODATUBES.why: Export-led SS seamless niche with an integrated mill and certifications, but tiny scale, negative cash flow, 211-day working-capital cycle and steel/freight-driven margin swings (Q1 FY27 PAT -26%).

MODISONLTD.why: ~60% share in silver electrical contacts with recycling edge, ROCE 31% and revenue doubling in Q1 FY27, but silver-price working-capital swings (FY26 CFO -₹64 Cr) keep it a notch below Shivalik's IP-led consistency.

SALZERELEC.why: ATEX-certified cam-switch niche and growing exports, but small scale, sub-10% ROE, rising debt and a Q1 FY27 margin collapse (EBITDA 6%, guidance cut to 8-8.5%) drop it below RR Kabel in the set.

BBL.why: 80-year transformer + HT-motor maker riding grid capex (order book ₹2,133 Cr) with an AA- balance sheet, but OPM down to 5.3%, negative FY26 operating cash flow, a delayed expansion and no investor calls leave it well behind Voltamp/TRIL on returns and execution.

LAKSELEC.why: Captive LMW panel maker: revenue recovering (+26% Q1 FY27) but margins near zero, very small, illiquid and dependent on one customer.

UNIVCABLES.why: One of few EHV cable makers with Birla backing, a ₹3,025 Cr order book and fast-growing exports, but small scale, ~10% margins, rising debt and sub-10% ROE versus Polycab/KEI.

GMDCLTD.why: Exclusive Gujarat lignite/bauxite leases with Odisha coal and rare-earth optionality (IREL MoU 31 Jul 2026), but mineral cyclicality, declining core lignite margins (FY26 OPM 17%) and pre-revenue diversification keep it mid-table.

EIMCOELECO.why: Near-monopoly underground LHD supplier to Coal India with a net-cash balance sheet, but monopsony customer, structurally declining underground mining and the Sept-2025 exit of JV partner Sandvik (now a pure competitor) keep it below the global majors and Tega.

TEGA.why: Global #2 in polymer mill-liners with IP and high switching cost but mining-capex cyclicality and a recent PAT dip.

GRAPHITE.why: One of two Indian UHP-electrode makers with a fortress balance sheet (₹3,939 Cr net cash) and 97% utilisation in Q1 FY27, but electrode-price cyclicality, exiting European operations and ROE of ~3% keep it mid-table.

HEG.why: India's largest electrode exporter with the world's biggest single-site plant at >90% utilisation, a 29% Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin recovery and a GrafTech stake; cyclical but best-positioned domestically, with anode optionality now housed in the demerged HEG Advanced Materials (effective 01-Sep-2026).

USHAMART.why: Global specialty wire-rope leader post-steel exit with a qualification moat, 20%+ EBITDA margin, 19% ROCE and net cash; behind only Bekaert on scale, with promoter-group selling the main blemish.

KAMDHENU.why: Asset-light franchise brand with 22% ROE, no debt and royalty income growing 25% (FY26) and 16% (Q1 FY27), but commodity-linked own manufacturing, a small base and low headline growth keep it behind the integrated majors.

MMP.why: Dominant Indian aluminium-powder/foil maker with Toyo Aluminium technology and a sharp Q1 FY27 rebound (+27% revenue), but LME-linked 8-9% margins, small scale, rising debt for T&D diversification and the Apr-2025 fatal fire keep it below the global specialists.

IFGLEXPOR.why: Specialised steel-refractory maker with exports but steel-capex cyclicality and mid-pack returns.

BOROSCI.why: Dominant Indian lab-glassware brand with 60-year trust and a net-cash balance sheet, but small scale (FY26 revenue ₹467 Cr), input-cost-driven margins and two divisions still in turnaround.

SIGNPOST.why: Municipal/transit-concession street-furniture moat with DOOH growth, 27% ROE and FY26 PAT +107%, but small, receivable-heavy (201 debtor days) and exposed to contract renewals; unlisted Pioneer Publicity swapped for listed transit-OOH peer Cash Ur Drive.

RKSWAMY.why: Integrated agency with PSU/BFSI relationships, research/data assets and Bharat reach; FY26 margins and cash flow recovered, but digital disruption, lumpy quarters and the holding-company model keep it mid-table.

QUESS.why: India's largest staffing platform, now debt-free with 24% ROCE (FY26) and a rising Professional/Overseas profit share, but a low-margin, working-capital-heavy model with an unresolved 80JJAA tax qualification.

CMSINFO.why: India's largest cash-management network (60% ATM cash share) with an RBI-regulated moat, debt-free balance sheet and now all three top private/PSU bank mandates; FY26 PAT -19% and the Aug-2026 guidance trim show cyclical pressure, while UPI stays the long-term threat.

best_own.name: CMS Info Systems
best_own.why: scale + recurring fixed-fee contracts, AA+ balance sheet

DIFFNKG.why: Fastest grower in the set (FY26 PAT +39%, Q1 FY27 revenue +36.5%, order book ₹209 Cr) with a differentiated heavy-engineering/wear-parts niche, but small, capex-cyclical and with weaker pricing power and cash conversion than Esab.

SHREEJISPG.why: Dry-bulk lighterage niche with high ROE and fast growth, but freight cyclicality, a one-year listing history and the ₹629 Cr Segal Ships admiralty claim (vessels arrested Dec 2025) cap the rank; defunct Mercator swapped for SME lighterage peer Seacoast.

avoid.name: Seacoast Shipping Services
avoid.why: sub-scale SME lighterage peer with thin margins

GESHIP.why: India's largest private shipper with a diversified fleet, ~$600 mn net cash, through-cycle quarterly dividends and now a ₹900 Cr buyback at ~0.8x NAV — best capital allocation in the set; ranks first despite freight cyclicality.

best_own.name: Great Eastern Shipping
best_own.why: balance sheet + dividends + buyback below NAV

SCI.why: India's only PSU shipper with sovereign cargo access, now earning record margins (Q1 FY27 EBITDA 48%) and being repositioned as a strategic national carrier instead of a privatisation candidate, but PSU inefficiency, board-composition fines and freight cyclicality keep it below GE Shipping.

NIFTYBEES.why: Oldest, most-liquid Nifty-50 ETF with tightest tracking and deepest on-exchange liquidity.

MON100.why: Largest, longest-track Nasdaq-100 onshore wrapper with reasonable tracking; subject to subscription caps.

MAFANG.why: Concentrated equal-weight FANG+ basket — higher beta and volatility than diversified Nasdaq-100/S&P wrappers.

AEROFLEX.set: SS flexible hoses / engineered flow products (India)
AEROFLEX.why: Only scaled Indian SS-flexible-hose maker with a BIS-QCO barrier, 50% five-year PAT CAGR and a fast-scaling data-centre skid franchise (Q1 FY27 revenue +72%, PAT +162%); leads the domestic set on growth and margin, capital efficiency (ROCE 19%) is the gap to global peers.

best_own.name: Aeroflex Industries
best_own.why: domestic monopoly + exports + data-centre liquid-cooling optionality

KENNAMET.why: Premium tungsten-carbide tooling with US-parent IP now showing 29% growth and 33% ROCE (FY26), moving ahead of Mitsubishi Materials in the set; still behind Sandvik/Iscar on owned R&D and scale, and cash conversion must catch up with reported profits.

HONAUT.why: #1 in DCS process automation with extreme switching costs and parent IP, but Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 1.8%, a 12.6% ROE and an illiquid stock keep it below ABB India.

SKFINDUS.why: Top-2 industrial bearing maker with a 34% high-margin aftermarket and 30% ROCE, growing 18% in Q1 FY27; Schaeffler leads on breadth and EV content, and SKF's margin is temporarily depressed by demerger costs and forex.

INGERRAND.why: US-parent brand with 43% ROE, 57% ROCE and 24% OPM, debt-free; FY26 was a soft year (PAT -4%) but Q1 FY27 sales +20% (13-Aug-2026) and the operational Sanand plant restore growth; still behind Atlas Copco on scale and Elgi on domestic growth.

KIRLPNU.why: Gas-compression and refrigeration leader with 30% ROCE, zero debt, AA rating and a ₹1,853 Cr order book, but niche scale and group-governance overhang keep it below the global compressor majors.

ISGEC.why: Multi-product boilers/presses/sugar-equipment with global reach but lumpy projects and low ROE.

JNKINDIA.why: Exclusive Korean fired-heater technology, FY26 revenue +72% and a ₹1,801 Cr order book with green-H2 optionality, but project-lumpy, working-capital heavy, margins down to 11-12% and a first order cancellation (16-Jul-2026).

POWERICA.why: Largest independent Cummins DG dealer with AMC recurring revenue, a ₹1,700 Cr order book led by data centres and a wind IPP annuity, but a 5.6% genset margin in Q1 FY27 shows dependence on Cummins/commodity pass-through, and grid-reliability is the long-term risk.

ENRIN.why: Gas-turbine + transformer/switchgear + HVDC franchise with parent technology, 68% ROCE and a ₹19,331 Cr backlog riding grid capex; ranks behind Hitachi Energy/ABB on HVDC-automation breadth, export autonomy and order-intake consistency.

CESC.why: Century-old Kolkata distribution monopoly now adding DISCOMs (Chandigarh) and a 4.5 GWp contracted renewable platform (ReNew 1.4 GWp deal, Aug-2026), with a 4% yield; regulated returns, rising debt and Malegaon losses keep it below Tata Power/Torrent on growth-quality.

GIPCL.why: Long-term GUVNL PPAs, captive lignite and a now-larger solar book (600 MW Khavda live, 500 MW coming) at 0.84x book, but leverage has jumped to 6.7x debt/EBITDA and a lignite expansion is proposed.

NLCINDIA.why: Lignite miner-genco with captive fuel cost edge, AAA rating and a now-complete 1,980 MW Ghatampur project, but polluting-fuel transition, rising leverage and PSU pace keep it below NTPC/NHPC and the hydro/solar-heavier peers.

SJVN.why: Hydro concessions plus a large under-construction book (1,561.5 MW hydro, 660 MW thermal, 1,705 MW solar) but long gestation, low ROE (4.6% FY26), 2.25x leverage and governance slippage (exchange fines 26-Aug-2026); FY27 commissioning of 2,284 MW is the swing factor.

PFC.why: Largest power-sector financier with sovereign-backed AAA funding, 21% ROE and GNPA down to 0.66% (Jun-26), but DISCOM credit risk, a flat Q1 FY27 loan book and spread compression cap quality; REC (to be merged into PFC from 01-Apr-2027) remains the cleaner book.

best_own.name: REC
best_own.why: similar moat, cleaner book; merging into PFC at 88:100 from 01-Apr-2027

PTC.why: Largest bilateral power trader plus cross-border flows, now net-cash with a ₹23 special dividend and PFS exit in motion, but thin trading margins (3.35 paise/unit), surcharge-income erosion and IEX disintermediation cap quality.

KPIGREEN.why: Fast-growing Gujarat IPP+CPP developer (FY26 PAT +57%, 6.94 GW portfolio, 1 GW+ energised IPP) but Q1 FY27 (11 Aug 2026) brought a 14% PAT drop under ₹5,197 Cr of debt, a growth-guide cut to ~30%, a CFO exit and a subsidiary auditor resignation, with 44.74% of the promoter stake pledged — well below the balance-sheet strength of Adani Green or Tata Power Renewables.

CLEANMAX.why: Leading C&I open-access developer with marquee hyperscaler clients and fully contracted growth (Q1 FY27 revenue +107%, CARE AA- upgrade 20 May 2026), but 4.76x leverage, ROE ~2% and ongoing early-investor exits (DSDG 3 Sep 2026) keep it below the large integrated renewables players; HOLD.

DEEDEV.why: IBR/ASME-certified high-pressure piping for refineries/power with a genuine capacity moat and a ₹2,428 Cr order book, but project-lumpy revenue, weak cash conversion, ROE ~9% and D/E ~0.9x (pre-prepayment) keep it below the diversified engineering majors.

SOUTHWEST.why: Diversified exploration/CBM/seismic driller with record ₹761 Cr order book, 24% OPM and ROCE 20%, but client concentration, 175-day debtors and Jun-26 promoter selling keep it below Deep Industries on quality.

GALAPREC.why: Branded precision spring/fastener exporter growing 20-30% with a ₹110 Cr order book and 17% OPM, but small scale, 180-day working capital and a pending Income Tax matter keep it below Sundram/Sansera.

HAPPYFORGE.why: Largest heavy-press line in India with 31% EBITDA margins, ₹950 Cr order book and record Q1 FY27; still behind Bharat Forge/Sundram on scale, defence/export breadth and customer diversification.

PITTIENG.why: GE/Siemens-qualified lamination maker with a rail, data-centre and mining tailwind and a raised FY27 guide (11 Aug 2026), but CRGO-steel margins, heavy capex leverage and a falling ROCE (15%) keep it mid-table.

TEJASNET.why: Only Indian end-to-end telecom-gear IP with Tata backing and a renewed BSNL 4G order (₹1,537 Cr LoI, 27 Aug 2026), but severe revenue lumpiness (FY26 -88%), continuing losses and ₹4,277 Cr net debt funding BSNL receivables keep it below the global majors.

WELCORP.why: Only Indian SAW+ERW maker with US and Saudi plants; record ₹24,750 Cr order book, 18.5% Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin and net cash ₹2,336 Cr (24-Jul-2026) lift it level with Jindal SAW, but steel/oil-cycle margins, weak DI demand and one-off-heavy PAT keep it below Tenaris.

SUZLON.why: Turnaround with 40% ROE, net cash ₹2,322 Cr and a record 6.1 GW order book, but Q1 FY27 (28 Jul 2026) showed EPC-led margin dilution (EBITDA margin 15.6%), cash conversion is weak and past governance scars plus an 11.7% promoter stake cap the score.

HLEGLAS.why: #2 glass-lined and #1 filter-dryer maker with a record ₹713.8 Cr order book and falling debt, but Q1 FY27 (10 Aug 2026) EBITDA margin of 7.5% and PAT of ₹2.1 Cr, a 3.2% glass-lined EBIT margin and the loss-making Omeras unit drop it below Standard Glass Lining in the peer set.

WENDT.why: Niche super-abrasives maker with a debt-free AA- balance sheet, Murugappa parentage and a Q1 FY27 rebound (revenue +36.6%, PAT +63.5%, 24 Jul 2026), but sub-scale (FY26 revenue ₹236 Cr), post-3M-exit margins of 13.6-15.4% vs 23% historically and ROE 4.9% keep it last in a strong peer set.

avoid.name: Wendt India
avoid.why: sub-scale; margin reset after May-2025 3M exit

SGIL.why: Niche 30 MT wind-casting supplier with a ₹600 Cr executable order book and 6 global OEM approvals, but the Q1 FY27 loss of ₹10.1 Cr (13 Aug 2026), borrowings of ~₹243 Cr on ₹101 Cr net worth, sub-1x interest cover and 8.4x book keep it last; HOLD retained only because the ₹500 Cr FY27 guide was maintained and July utilisation was 85%+.

avoid.name: Synergy Green Industries
avoid.why: await deleveraging and proof of the FY27 ramp

KSB.why: German-parent pumps/valves franchise with a unique nuclear position, debt-free balance sheet and ROCE 25%, but H1 CY26 PAT fell 20% with OPM at 8-12% and receivables stretched; the Q2 CY26 (4 Aug 2026) order haul and ₹2,744 Cr backlog support HOLD rather than ADD at ~54x P/E.

JYOTICNC.why: #1 listed Indian CNC OEM with an aerospace/defence-heavy ₹4,848 Cr order book, 18% ROE and standalone growth of 37% (Q1 FY27, 7 Aug 2026), but the unresolved Huron probe, weak FY26 cash conversion and a promoter pledge (Aug-2026) keep it at HOLD rather than ADD at ~73x earnings.

3MINDIA.why: Parent-tech diversified portfolio with 29% ROE and strong cash but premium valuation and an MNC-royalty drag.

VASCONEQ.why: Small RE+EPC with a Pune land bank but heavy losses, negative OCF and a weak balance sheet.

RAYMOND.why: Now a focused aerospace/precision-components play with a ₹5,960 Cr ten-year aerospace order book and net cash, but sub-scale aerospace revenue (₹123 Cr/quarter), ROCE ~3% during transition and a weaker governance record than Bharat Forge or Sundram Fasteners.

avoid.name: Raymond
avoid.why: low ROE until aerospace capex earns; governance history

RAYMONDREL.why: Thane township with irreplaceable land, the Raymond brand and a JDA book now driving 64% of sales; FY26 PAT ₹305 Cr and Q1 FY27 pre-sales +129% show execution, but MMR-only concentration, growth cash burn and the family-governance perception keep it behind the majors.

RUSTOMJEE.why: Trusted MMR brand with a JDA/redevelopment-led asset-light model, FY26 pre-sales ₹4,022 Cr (+33%) and AA- ratings, but reported ROE of 2.8%, negative statutory OCF and launch-dependent bookings keep it below Oberoi/Lodha/Godrej.

ELDEHSG.why: 40-year UP/Lucknow brand with record FY26 bookings (+120%), 37% Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin and a 3.4 msf pipeline, but small, single-city and increasingly land-owning rather than asset-light.

ASHIANA.why: Disciplined, net-cash mid-income developer and senior-living first-mover (FY26 pre-sales ₹2,421 Cr, ROE 15%, realisation +37% in Q1 FY27) but small parcels, lumpy revenue and a guided FY27-FY28 pre-sales dip keep it behind the large diversified developers.

EMBDL.why: Embassy brand and a large paid land bank now delivering record pre-sales (₹4,631 Cr FY26, Q1 FY27 +338%), but negative ROE, 64.9% promoter pledge, expensive debt and litigation overhang keep it last among listed developers.

avoid.name: Embassy Developments
avoid.why: await positive OCF and pledge reduction before adding

TREL.why: Allcargo-demerged logistics-park and land-bank play — debt-free, CARE A- (May-26), promoter buying — but small, lumpy, sub-4% ROCE and early-stage on its ₹700 Cr pipeline; unlisted Welspun One swapped for listed Brookfield India REIT.

OMINFRAL.why: Dam/hydro EPC plus toll and SRA realty optionality but lumpy projects, negative OCF and losses.

INTERARCH.why: #2 PEB maker with in-house design, zero debt, a record FY26 and a ₹1,864 Cr order book skewed to new-age industries, but steel-price-exposed 8.6-10% margins, a negative-CFO FY26 and QIP dilution keep it level with Pennar and behind Tata BlueScope's steel integration.

CAPACITE.why: Mivan-formwork high-rise specialist for tier-1 developers but developer-credit risk and a working-capital-heavy model.

ARIS.why: Tech-enabled construction-materials marketplace but loss-making, thin margins and working-capital-heavy vs better-funded peers.

SHANKARA.why: After the Sep-2025 demerger SBPL is a sub-scale South-India tube/roofing processor with 1.7% OPM, negative OCF and a SAST lapse; the ₹150 open offer (7–21 Sep 2026) is a reasonable exit window, hence TRIM.

best_own.name: APL Apollo Tubes
best_own.why: scale, DFT technology, best returns in structural tubes

WHIRLPOOL.why: Global-parent tech and washing-machine strength with revenue re-accelerating (+12% in Q1 FY27), but OPM collapsed to 5%, PAT fell ~30% in each of the last two quarters and the parent's sell-down (39.76%, target ~20%) overhangs the stock.

ABLBL.why: Premium apparel brands with retail scale and improving execution (Q1 FY27 LTL +8%, EBITDA margin 16%) post-demerger, but lease-heavy leverage, markdown risk and a discretionary slowdown keep it mid-table behind Trent and Page.

BOROLTD.why: Trusted borosilicate/opal brand with capacity-led volume growth, but low ROCE (11.5%), energy- and dumping-driven margin compression (14.6% in Q1 FY27) and negative FCF keep it below Hawkins, TTK and La Opala on quality.

ORIENTHOT.why: Taj-affiliated premium South-India assets with ADR upside and now low leverage, but regional concentration and a static portfolio; the 24 Aug 2026 merger converts the holding into IHCL stock (25 per 117) by H2 FY28, so HOLD through completion.

best_own.name: Indian Hotels (IHCL)
best_own.why: brand + pipeline + RoCE; acquirer of OHL

EIHOTEL.why: Oberoi/Trident — the cleanest luxury brand moat with irreplaceable assets and 9/10 pricing power (RGI 125, Q1 FY27); behind IHCL on scale, pipeline and 2026 margin momentum (EBITDA margin 29.7% vs 32.0%, Kolkata delayed to 2029).

best_own.name: Indian Hotels (IHCL)
best_own.why: scale + asset-light pipeline (Oriental Hotels merger announced 25 Aug 2026)

MSTCLTD.why: Trusted government e-auction franchise with 27% ROE, nil debt and a 54% payout, now free of legacy trading and growing e-commerce revenue 28% (Q1 FY27); still policy-linked with scrap/coal exposure, behind IRCTC's captive monopoly.

INCAP.why: Now verified as a ₹27 Cr-revenue capacitor micro-cap with 2% ROE, a 46% revenue drop in Q1 FY27 and a ~138x P/E — lowest-quality in the set; TRIM into liquidity given no growth engine.

avoid.name: Incap
avoid.why: sub-scale commodity capacitors, shrinking revenue, 2% ROE

AVTNPL.why: Global leader in marigold/lutein with a clean-label tailwind and re-accelerating growth (FY26 +28%, Q1 FY27 +82%); trails unlisted majors Synthite/Plant Lipids on scale and breadth and carries heavy customer concentration.

BEPL.why: Domestic ABS duopoly economics, debt-free with a self-funded expansion to 100,000 MTPA (Sep-2026) and Q1 FY27 revenue +53%, but sub-scale and less diversified than Supreme Petrochem.

CENTENKA.why: Clean Birla lineage and net-cash balance sheet with a record Q1 FY27 (volumes +12%), but commoditised nylon yarn with 7-10% normalised margins and weak returns versus diversified SRF/Sanathan.

CYIENT.why: Strong aerospace/rail/geospatial niches and clean governance, but DET revenue was flat in constant currency in Q1 FY27 and margins (13.2%) trail LTTS/Tata Elxsi, keeping it fifth in the set.

ELECON.why: Dominant Indian gear franchise with the largest installed base, net cash and a record ₹1,518 Cr order book (Jun-26); margin slippage and conservative FY27 guidance narrow but do not remove its lead over Shanthi Gears.

EPIGRAL.why: Best-integrated derivatives mix (CPVC/ECH/chlorotoluenes, epoxy next) among mid-cap chlor-alkali peers with CRISIL AA and ND/EBITDA 0.8x; trails only diversified Grasim, and FY26's flat, lower-margin year keeps it level with DCM Shriram.

GPPL.why: Well-governed Maersk-run port with net cash, ~100% payout and improving execution (FY26 PAT +30%, Q1 FY27 underlying revenue +20%), but far smaller and slower-growing than APSEZ/JSW and dependent on the Sep-2028 concession extension now in process.

LCL.why: Global leader in raffia machinery with a strong aftermarket, ROCE 41% and a ₹1,778 Cr order book (Jun-26); narrower breadth than Starlinger/W&H and only one quarter of listed history.

RAMRAT.why: Scaled winding-wire brand now growing fastest in the set (Q1 FY27 revenue +89%, ROCE 24%) via copper tubes, but thin 4.8% margins, rising debt and negative FY26 cash flow keep Precision Wires the higher-quality pure-play.

RATNAMANI.why: Highest-quality SS/CS pipe franchise with global approvals, net cash and best-in-class cash conversion (CFO/OP 147% FY26); lead over Welspun/Jindal SAW narrowed by two years of revenue decline and ROCE compression to 18%.

RSYSTEMS.why: Blackstone backing and AI-led product engineering lifted growth to +30% (Q2 CY26) with 20% adjusted margins, but scale, organic-growth visibility and earnings clarity still trail Persistent/Coforge.

SIMPLEXCAS.why: Sub-scale castings maker whose FY26/Q1 FY27 numbers (OPM 18-19%, ROCE 24%, sales +35%) are improving, but weak cash conversion, dilutive funding and the Aug-2026 CRISIL non-cooperation flag keep it the weakest name in the set.

avoid.name: Simplex Castings
avoid.why: sub-scale, weak cash conversion, rating flag

TIMETECHNO.why: Category leader in drums/IBCs with a fast-growing composite-cylinder vector (+29.3% in Q1 FY27) and a deleveraged balance sheet, but ROE of 13% and weak FY26 cash conversion keep it well behind Supreme on returns.

TMCV.why: CV market leader gaining share (36.8% in Q1 FY27, HCV 56.3%) with Tata-group governance, 68% auto ROCE and net cash; the Iveco acquisition (Oct/Nov 2026) is the swing factor for returns and leverage.

ZENSARTECH.why: Net-cash RPG-group mid-cap with a record BFSI deal, but FY26 cc growth of 1.7%, a Q1 FY27 margin reset to 14.6% and shrinking TMT/HLS books keep it behind Persistent/Coforge on growth consistency.

BEL.why: Dominant defence-electronics PSU with a ₹72,258 Cr order book, net cash, 36% ROCE and Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 25% (27 Jul 2026); FY27 guidance reaffirmed, so HOLD despite the ~49x multiple and QRSAM timing risk.

IKS.why: High-quality physician-enterprise RCM platform (FY26 OPM 34%, ROE 40%) with sticky US clients, now the only India-listed peer owning a US hospital EHR system of record after TruBridge (9 Jul 2026); scale still trails R1 RCM and the debt-funded deal adds integration risk, so HOLD.

INOXWIND.why: Turnaround wind OEM with a 4.4 GW backlog and improving margins (adj. EBITDA ~27% Q1 FY27), but flat revenue, PAT -34% (7 Aug 2026), negative FY26 cash flow and guidance misses leave it behind Suzlon on scale, execution and balance sheet; HOLD pending H2 FY27 delivery.

INVPRECQ.why: Niche investment-castings maker with improving quality (OPM 20.7% Q1 FY27, CARE BBB upgrade 9 Jul 2026) but sub-scale versus diversified Bharat Forge and behind PTC Industries on aerospace super-alloy positioning; HOLD given the ~86x multiple.

IONEXCHANG.why: Still the only integrated resin-to-EPC-to-consumer water platform in India with a ₹2,473 Cr order book and the ₹500 Cr Hyundai win, but Q4 FY26/Q1 FY27 margin collapse (OPM 2.3%/4.5%), negative cash flow and open governance items drop it below Thermax and Wabag on quality; HOLD pending margin recovery.

best_own.name: Thermax (broader)
best_own.why: profitable water franchise in a diversified, cash-rich group

LOKESHMACH.why: Small SPM/CNC maker whose defence optionality is now backed by a ₹58 Cr MoD order and the 30 Jun 2026 OFAC delisting, but sub-scale, low-return and heavily indebted versus LMW/Jyoti CNC; HOLD at a 179x multiple.

RATNAVEER.why: Niche SS finished-products maker growing 20%+ (Q1 FY27 record ₹315 Cr revenue) with CCL optionality, but thin ~10% margins, negative FCF and repeated dilution keep it well behind integrated Jindal Stainless; HOLD through the Sep-2026 rights issue and Nov-2026 CCL commissioning.

VIPULORG.why: Small pigment/dye/food-colour maker now with commissioned Sayakha capacity (20 Aug 2026) and a membrane option; still sub-scale versus pigment leader Sudarshan and earning only ~8% ROCE.

AGI.why: Scaled, profitable and now near-debt-free container-glass leader (ROCE 19.6%, Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 22.3%) with premium/closures optionality; trails only unlisted Piramal Glass on premium breadth, while HNG remains distressed under its INSCO takeover.

ASAHIINDIA.why: Dominant OEM auto-glass share with AGC technology and float integration in a near-duopoly with Saint-Gobain; Q1 FY27 margin recovery (EBITDA 23%) and the QIP-funded deleveraging reinforce the lead, though ROE of ~10% still lags its moat.

MMFL.why: Solid mid-tier CV/export forger with a 67% machined mix and +18% FY27 growth guidance, but sub-scale, more levered (borrowings ₹1,235 Cr, ROCE 9%) and more cyclical than Bharat Forge, Ramkrishna or Happy Forgings.

BBOX.why: Largest and most global of the listed Indian integrators with the best hyperscaler exposure and a record US$950 mn backlog, but its 9% margin and weak FY25-FY26 cash conversion rank it below Netweb's higher-margin, cash-generative AI-server franchise.

best_own.name: Netweb Technologies
best_own.why: higher margins, net cash and direct AI-compute exposure

avoid.name: Sterlite Technologies
avoid.why: leverage and loss history in optical/network services

SIGNATURE.why: Volume leader in Gurugram affordable/mid housing with a clean balance sheet after the RMZ deal, but weaker earnings quality, a single micro-market and a soft Q1 FY27 leave it well behind DLF's annuity-backed, net-cash NCR franchise and Godrej's diversified launch engine.

best_own.name: DLF
best_own.why: net-cash NCR leader with rental annuity and premium brand

avoid.name: Omaxe
avoid.why: stretched balance sheet and delayed NCR deliveries

SOFTTECH.set: Indian small/mid-cap vertical software and GovTech
SOFTTECH.why: Owns a genuinely defensible municipal-software niche and is growing revenue faster than most peers, but its sub-₹10 Cr profits, capitalised-R&D earnings quality and 18.9% promoter stake place it below cash-generative product companies such as Newgen and Nucleus.

best_own.name: Newgen Software Technologies
best_own.why: scaled, cash-generative product platform with global enterprise and government clients

avoid.name: Kellton Tech Solutions
avoid.why: acquisition-heavy, low-margin services model with weak cash conversion

SUNDRMFAST.why: Best balance sheet and governance in the set (D/E 0.11x, A1+, 28% payout) with a broadening non-auto book, but a slower historical growth rate and commodity-like core product keep it a notch below Bharat Forge's defence/aerospace optionality and Endurance's European aluminium franchise.

best_own.name: Bharat Forge
best_own.why: larger defence/aerospace and industrial optionality with global scale

E2E.set: India-listed AI / cloud and data-centre infrastructure
E2E.why: The only listed Indian pure-play GPU cloud with the fastest growth in the set (Q1 FY27 revenue +334%) and a ₹1,000 Cr anchor contract, but its balance-sheet dependence on repeated equity raises, single-vendor exposure and ~396x multiple rank it below Tata Communications' diversified, cash-generative digital-infrastructure franchise and Netweb's asset-light AI-server business.

best_own.name: Tata Communications
best_own.why: diversified digital-infrastructure cash flows with data-centre and AI exposure at a fraction of the multiple

avoid.name: Sterlite Technologies
avoid.why: leverage and loss history in optical/network services

LAURUSLABS.why: Fastest CDMO growth and the sharpest margin recovery in the Indian API/CDMO set (Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 31.8%, CDMO +69%), with AA-rated balance sheet; ranks below Divi's on scale, net cash and margin consistency and roughly level with Syngene on quality, ahead on growth.

best_own.name: Divi's Laboratories
best_own.why: net-cash, 30%+ margins and unmatched scale in custom synthesis

avoid.name: Aarti Drugs
avoid.why: commoditised API portfolio with thin margins and low pricing power

FORCEMOT.why: Dominant in its passenger-van niche with the best balance sheet and ROCE in the group, but far smaller, more concentrated (one platform, two engine customers) and less generous to minorities than the diversified CV leaders Eicher, Ashok Leyland and Tata Motors.

best_own.name: Eicher Motors
best_own.why: Royal Enfield cash engine plus VECV CV franchise with consistent payouts

avoid.name: Olectra Greentech
avoid.why: e-bus order execution and working-capital risk

HINDWAREAP.why: Strong sanitaryware brand but the weakest balance sheet and profitability in the set - two loss years, ~4x leverage and a BBB+ (RWD) rating versus debt-free Cera and the scaled, cash-generative pipe leaders Astral and Supreme; the pending demerger is the main re-rating lever.

best_own.name: Cera Sanitaryware
best_own.why: debt-free direct sanitaryware/faucet peer with consistent margins and payouts

avoid.name: Prince Pipes & Fittings
avoid.why: sub-scale pipes player facing the same resin and competition squeeze with weaker brand pull

KIRLOSENG.set: Indian engines, gensets and power solutions
KIRLOSENG.why: Second-largest listed Indian genset franchise with a strong aftermarket and new data-centre/DEUTZ growth levers, but weaker margins (11-18% vs Cummins' ~20%+), an NBFC-cluttered balance sheet and family-dispute overhang rank it clearly behind Cummins India and below Triveni's cash-rich turbine niche.

best_own.name: Cummins India
best_own.why: higher margins, net cash, parent technology and data-centre genset leadership

avoid.name: Greaves Cotton
avoid.why: losses in the electric-mobility subsidiary and weak core engine demand

MAXESTATES.set: Delhi-NCR and pan-India listed real-estate developers
MAXESTATES.why: Max Estates has the fastest pre-sales growth in this set (+5x YoY in Q1 FY27) but the smallest scale, the thinnest reported profits and the highest leverage relative to rental income; Oberoi and DLF pair scale with 17% ROCE (Oberoi) and deep annuity portfolios.

best_own.name: Oberoi Realty
best_own.why: Highest ROCE (17.3%) and margin discipline among listed developers, low leverage and a proven Mumbai annuity portfolio.

avoid.name: Signature Global (India)
avoid.why: Mid-income NCR volume play with thin margins and higher leverage; most exposed if NCR absorption slows.

MCX.set: Indian capital-market infrastructure (exchanges, depositories, RTAs, brokers)
MCX.why: MCX is the only true monopoly in the set (>99% share) with the highest margins (72% EBITDA) and fastest growth, but its volumes are the most concentrated in two asset classes; BSE and CDSL have similar regulatory moats with more diversified flows.

best_own.name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India
best_own.why: Highest margin, debt-free, near-monopoly franchise with regulatory tailwinds still opening new participant categories; the set's best business despite a full valuation.

avoid.name: Angel One
avoid.why: Discount broker exposed to SEBI's equity-F&O curbs and pricing pressure; lowest moat and most cyclical earnings in the set.

SCHNEIDER.set: Indian T&D / medium-voltage electrical equipment makers
SCHNEIDER.why: Schneider Infra has the weakest margins (5% OPM in Q1 FY27) and the only leveraged balance sheet among the MNC T&D peers, offset by a strong parent and record orders; ABB and Hitachi Energy earn 25-30%+ ROCE with net cash.

best_own.name: ABB India
best_own.why: Net cash, ~30% ROCE, a diversified electrification and automation portfolio and consistent dividends — the quality benchmark of the set.

avoid.name: BHEL
avoid.why: Thermal-power legacy, low single-digit margins and working-capital-heavy PSU execution.

ANANTRAJ.set: Delhi-NCR and pan-India listed real-estate developers
ANANTRAJ.why: Anant Raj offers the best margins (OPM 26-29%) and lowest leverage among NCR developers plus a unique data-centre option, but its 11% ROE and 39x P/E trail Oberoi's returns and DLF's scale and annuity depth.

best_own.name: Oberoi Realty
best_own.why: Highest ROCE (17.3%) and margin discipline among listed developers, low leverage and a proven Mumbai annuity portfolio.

avoid.name: Signature Global (India)
avoid.why: Mid-income NCR volume play with thin margins and higher leverage; most exposed if NCR absorption slows.

MARINE.set: Indian LV/MV switchgear and power-distribution equipment makers
MARINE.why: Marine has the fastest growth in the set (revenue +53% in Q1 FY27) but the weakest cash conversion, smallest scale and thinnest disclosure; ABB, Siemens and CG Power combine scale, net cash and 20-30% ROCE.

best_own.name: ABB India
best_own.why: Net cash, ~30% ROCE, a diversified electrification and automation portfolio and consistent dividends — the quality benchmark of the set.

avoid.name: Salzer Electronics
avoid.why: Low-margin wires and switchgear assembler with weak pricing power and modest returns on capital.

STYRENIX.set: Indian styrenics and commodity polymer producers
STYRENIX.why: Styrenix is the only listed Indian ABS-plus-PS producer with an overseas plant, but its earnings are the most spread-sensitive in the set and its promoter has sold down; Supreme Petrochem offers net cash and steadier polystyrene/EPS returns.

best_own.name: Supreme Petrochem
best_own.why: Net-cash polystyrene/EPS leader with consistent 20%+ ROCE and steady dividends.

avoid.name: Apcotex Industries
avoid.why: Synthetic-rubber and latex maker facing import-led margin compression and weak volume growth.

BEML.set: Indian construction/mining equipment and rolling-stock makers
BEML.why: BEML has the broadest product set and the largest order book relative to sales in the group, but the lowest ROCE (8%), the longest receivable cycle (191 days) and the most volatile margins; ACE and Escorts Kubota earn 25-30%+ ROCE with net cash.

best_own.name: Action Construction Equipment
best_own.why: Crane market leader with 31.6% ROCE, net cash and consistent margin delivery.

avoid.name: Texmaco Rail & Engineering
avoid.why: Thin single-digit margins, a working-capital-heavy wagon business and weak returns on capital.

KIRLOSBROS.set: Indian pump and fluid-handling equipment makers
KIRLOSBROS.why: KBL has the broadest range and the strongest balance sheet after KSB, but flat earnings, low-margin overseas units and the family dispute keep it a notch below KSB's MNC-backed consistency; WPIL and Shakti are more project- or subsidy-dependent.

best_own.name: KSB Ltd
best_own.why: German-parent technology, 20%+ ROCE, net cash and steady margin delivery across industrial and energy pumps.

avoid.name: Shakti Pumps (India)
avoid.why: Earnings tied to PM-KUSUM solar-pump subsidy tenders with state-government receivables and policy-timing risk.

ASHAPURMIN.set: Indian listed mining and industrial-minerals companies
ASHAPURMIN.why: Ashapura's Guinea volume growth and 20% ROCE beat most domestic miners on growth, but it lacks the reserve ownership, net-cash balance sheets and dividend records of NMDC, MOIL or GMDC and carries country, freight and pledge risks; it ranks above only 20 Microns, its closest industrial-minerals competitor.

best_own.name: NMDC
best_own.why: largest iron-ore miner with owned reserves, net cash and a consistent dividend record

avoid.name: 20 Microns
avoid.why: thin margins and leverage in commodity industrial minerals

CHOLAHLDNG.why: Second only to Bajaj Holdings among listed financial holdcos on the quality and growth of the underlying franchise (CIFCL ROE 21%, AUM +23%) and group governance; ranked below Bajaj Holdings for its token payout, insurance underwriting losses and a discount that has not narrowed.

best_own.name: Bajaj Holdings & Investment
best_own.why: stakes in Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv and Bajaj Auto with a large treasury and meaningful dividends

avoid.name: JSW Holdings
avoid.why: single-asset steel holdco with minimal payout and poor liquidity

GLENMARK.why: Glenmark's India growth (1.5x IPM) and specialty optionality (RYALTRIS, ISB 2001) are competitive, but its five-year ROE of 2%, repeated exceptional charges and US litigation history place it below Sun, Cipla, Zydus and Lupin on quality and consistency; the net-cash reset and 20%+ margins narrow the gap.

best_own.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries
best_own.why: largest India franchise plus a scaled global specialty business with consistent cash generation

avoid.name: Alembic Pharmaceuticals
avoid.why: US generics pricing pressure and sub-par returns on heavy capex

GMRP&UI.set: Indian private power generators and diversified infra (thermal IPPs, smart metering)
GMRP&UI.why: Ranks near the bottom of listed private power peers: operating assets are sound (PLFs 87-90%) but the pledged, diluting promoter, 1.2x interest cover and settlement-dependent profits compare poorly with JSW Energy's and Torrent's investment-grade balance sheets and steady payouts. Fresh evidence is strong enough to justify TRIM rather than the default HOLD.

best_own.name: JSW Energy
best_own.why: renewables-led growth on an investment-grade balance sheet with clean promoter ownership

avoid.name: Reliance Power
avoid.why: history of debt defaults and weak governance

HAL.set: Listed Indian defence primes (aerospace, electronics, shipbuilding, ordnance)
HAL.why: Widest moat and largest order book in the set, but ranked below Bharat Electronics on execution consistency and governance (BEL delivers to guidance with a diversified programme mix) and below Solar Industries on growth and private-sector agility; ahead of shipyards and missile makers on scale, ROCE and annuity-like ROH revenue.

best_own.name: Bharat Electronics
best_own.why: consistent delivery to guidance, diversified electronics order book, cleaner PSU execution record

avoid.name: Bharat Dynamics
avoid.why: lumpy missile-programme revenue with a history of delivery slippage and supply-chain dependence

OBEROIRLTY.why: Highest margins (56% OPM FY26) and cleanest ownership in the set, with a new NCR growth leg; ranked below DLF's scale and annuity depth and just below Godrej's pan-India pre-sales engine because of MMR concentration, lumpy revenue and a very thin float.

best_own.name: DLF
best_own.why: largest land bank, NCR leadership and DCCDL annuity portfolio

avoid.name: Sunteck Realty
avoid.why: sub-scale, lumpy MMR sales and weaker cash generation

SJS.set: Indian auto-component suppliers (interiors, aesthetics, lighting & electronics)
SJS.why: Best-in-set margins (30% EBITDA in Q1 FY27) and ROCE (28.6%) with a net-cash balance sheet, behind only Uno Minda's scale and product breadth. Ranked below Uno Minda because of the narrower product niche, low promoter holding and a rich valuation.

best_own.name: Uno Minda
best_own.why: largest diversified platform with EV/electronics breadth

avoid.name: Lumax Auto Technologies
avoid.why: thinnest margins in the set and more complex group/JV structure

SMLMAH.why: SML has the best return ratios in the set (ROCE 31%) and a strong parent, but lacks the scale, truck range and pricing power of Eicher/VECV, Ashok Leyland and Tata Motors; the pending related-party acquisition adds execution and governance uncertainty, and the valuation is the richest among peers.

best_own.name: Eicher Motors (VE Commercial Vehicles)
best_own.why: premium CV/bus franchise with Volvo technology plus the Royal Enfield cash engine

avoid.name: Olectra Greentech
avoid.why: tender-dependent e-bus order book with execution delays and thin cash generation

VIMTALABS.set: Contract research and testing laboratories (India-listed and global TIC majors)
VIMTALABS.why: Vimta has the best return profile among Indian listed labs (ROCE 25%, debt-free, 35% margins) but lacks the scale, network density and pricing power of the global TIC majors and Syngene's integrated CRO-CDMO platform; Q1 FY27 growth slipped below target.

best_own.name: Eurofins Scientific
best_own.why: global scale in food, environment and biopharma testing with acquisition-led network density

avoid.name: Choksi Laboratories
avoid.why: micro-cap with thin margins and limited accreditation breadth

SHRIPISTON.set: Auto Components - diversified engine, driveline and interior suppliers
SHRIPISTON.why: SPR Auto ranks mid-table: it has the highest ROCE (20.8%) and fastest TTM sales growth (+35%) in this set at a lower P/E (36x vs 48-94x for peers), but its franchise is more ICE-concentrated than Uno Minda or Schaeffler and its margins are being reset by the Antolin acquisition. HOLD as a fresh position pending Q2 FY27 evidence of margin normalisation.

best_own.name: Uno Minda
best_own.why: Broadest powertrain-agnostic portfolio (lighting, switches, alloy wheels, EV systems) with 19.7% ROCE and consistent content-per-vehicle gains; structurally less EV-transition risk than SPR.

avoid.name: Bharat Forge
avoid.why: Screener peer table (4 Sep 2026) shows latest-quarter consolidated net loss of Rs -90 Cr (-58% YoY) at a 94x P/E, with heavy export/defence cyclicality; weakest near-term earnings visibility in the set.

M&M.why: M&M leads the set on growth (Q1 FY27 PAT +34%, ROE 23%) and holds No.1 positions in SUVs, tractors, small LCVs and e-3Ws, whereas Maruti has superior balance-sheet strength but has been ceding SUV share. HOLD rather than ADD as a fresh holding because auto margins are at a cyclical trough and the stock's 1-year de-rating (-9%) reflects FII selling that may persist.

best_own.name: Mahindra & Mahindra
best_own.why: Within this peer set it combines the widest moat (dual leadership in SUVs and tractors), the highest ROE (23% annualised Q1 FY27) and the clearest EV leadership (XEV 9S top-selling EV), at a lower P/E (20.6x) than Maruti.

avoid.name: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles
avoid.why: Earnings dominated by JLR's tariff and production disruptions (Sep-2025 cyber-attack halt) while domestic PV share has slipped against M&M and Maruti; weakest visibility in the set.

WINDLAS.set: Indian pharma CDMO and contract-manufacturing mid/small caps
WINDLAS.why: Windlas is the cleanest balance sheet in the set (net cash, A+ rated, buyback plus 20% payout) and has grown revenue for 14 straight quarters, but its 11-12% margins and 12% ROE trail fermentation-CDMO Concord Biotech and OTC exporter Marksans, and it lacks Akums' scale. HOLD as a fresh position until Plant 6 utilisation and margin recovery are visible.

best_own.name: Concord Biotech
best_own.why: Fermentation-based API/CDMO with structurally higher margins and returns than oral-solid formulation CDMOs, and a regulated-market customer base; the highest-quality compounding franchise in the set.

avoid.name: Indoco Remedies
avoid.why: Loss-making FY25 with US regulatory (USFDA) remediation costs and elevated leverage; weakest earnings visibility and balance sheet in the set.

ELANTAS.set: Indian specialty-chemical niche leaders and MNC subsidiaries
ELANTAS.why: Elantas matches the niche leaders on balance sheet (zero debt) and returns (ROCE 21%) and is growing faster right now (Q2 CY26 sales +35%), but ranks mid-table because of its opaque MNC-subsidiary governance, 3-4% payout and 55x multiple. HOLD as a fresh holding until at least one more quarter confirms the new margin level.

best_own.name: Vinati Organics
best_own.why: Debt-free global leader in ATBS/IBB with a long record of 25%+ ROCE, founder-led capital allocation and meaningful dividends - the cleanest compounder in the set.

avoid.name: Sudarshan Chemical Industries
avoid.why: Leverage and integration risk from the 2025 Heubach pigments acquisition in a cyclical, price-competitive pigment market; weakest balance sheet in the set.

WABAG.set: Indian water and environmental infrastructure EPC / O&M
WABAG.why: Wabag has the largest and most international order book, the deepest desalination technology and a net-cash balance sheet, but its receivable intensity, other-income reliance and 19% promoter stake keep it just behind Ion Exchange, whose resin-chemicals franchise gives steadier cash flows. HOLD for a fresh holding: strong visibility, but wait for core-margin (ex-other income) and cash-conversion evidence in H2 FY27.

best_own.name: Ion Exchange (India)
best_own.why: Combines proprietary ion-exchange resin chemicals and consumer products with water EPC, giving higher-quality recurring cash flows, a net-cash balance sheet and 40%+ promoter holding.

avoid.name: Denta Water & Infra Solutions
avoid.why: Recently listed (Jan 2025) with revenue concentrated in Karnataka groundwater-recharge projects and a handful of government clients; weakest diversification and shortest track record in the set.

IRIS.set: Indian listed software-product and SaaS small/mid caps
IRIS.why: IRIS is the smallest and currently the only loss-making operator in this set; its regulator franchise and net cash keep it above AVOID, but Newgen, Intellect, RateGain and Nucleus all combine scale with sustained profitability. HOLD rather than TRIM only because cash of ~Rs 170 Cr underpins roughly a third of the market cap; revisit if H1 FY27 shows no margin recovery.

best_own.name: Newgen Software Technologies
best_own.why: Profitable, cash-generative low-code/ECM platform vendor with 20%+ margins, global BFSI clients and consistent dividends - the quality benchmark for Indian software products.

avoid.name: Brightcom Group
avoid.why: Subject to SEBI orders over accounting irregularities and promoter conduct, with trading restrictions and unreliable financials; uninvestable on governance grounds.

PURVA.set: South and west India listed residential developers
PURVA.why: Puravankara ranks last in its Bengaluru-centric peer set: comparable brand heritage but the weakest balance sheet (interest cover near 1x, IND A- versus AA-range peers), the lowest ROE and a record of launch delays and RERA extensions. TRIM: the Q1 FY27 operating rebound is encouraging, but a fresh holding with a critical leverage flag warrants reduced exposure until debt actually falls by the guided Rs 700 Cr and coverage exceeds 1.5x.

best_own.name: Brigade Enterprises
best_own.why: Bengaluru leader with a diversified residential, office, retail and hospitality portfolio generating annuity income, moderate leverage and a consistent delivery record - the quality counterpart to Puravankara's geography.

avoid.name: Shriram Properties
avoid.why: Mid-income focus with thin margins, sub-10% ROE and a history of guidance revisions; least attractive risk-reward among the remaining peers, though its leverage is now lower than Puravankara's.

ERIS.set: India domestic branded formulations (chronic-focused mid caps)
ERIS.why: Eris matches peers on chronic focus and margin but sits mid-table because its ROCE (14% FY26) and leverage (net debt ~Rs 2,300 Cr) are weaker than Torrent, Mankind or JB, and its FY27 guidance is already under pressure. Fresh holding, evidence mixed: HOLD.

best_own.name: Torrent Pharmaceuticals
best_own.why: Largest chronic-heavy India franchise with consistent 30%-plus EBITDA margins, strong cash generation and a longer record of integrating acquisitions profitably.

avoid.name: Indoco Remedies
avoid.why: Weakest in the set: FY25 losses, USFDA compliance problems at its Goa plants and an acute-heavy, low-margin domestic portfolio.

ABREL.why: ABREL has the parentage, balance sheet and land bank of a top-tier developer but not yet the sales run-rate: FY26 bookings of Rs 8,136 Cr were flat while DLF, Lodha and Godrej kept compounding, and Q1 FY27 was weak. Ranked mid-table; HOLD pending H2 FY27 launches.

best_own.name: DLF
best_own.why: Largest land bank, rental annuity via DLF Cyber City and consistent pre-sales growth with a net-cash residential business.

avoid.name: Puravankara
avoid.why: Highest leverage in the set with recent losses and slower collections; weakest balance sheet in a cyclical sector.

MAXIND.set: Indian listed healthcare services and senior-living operators
MAXIND.why: Max India is the only loss-making, cash-consuming name in this set; hospital peers earn 15-25% ROCE while Antara is 8-10 quarters from care-home unit profitability. It is a speculative option on senior care rather than a compounding franchise, so it ranks last. Fresh holding, evidence mixed on inflection: HOLD, not ADD.

best_own.name: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise
best_own.why: Largest integrated healthcare platform with hospitals, pharmacy and home-care, consistent profitability and the scale to enter senior care if it chooses.

avoid.name: Shalby
avoid.why: Weakest of the hospital peers: thin margins, losses in its implants venture and slower occupancy recovery.

EXIDEIND.set: Indian battery / energy-storage and auto-component majors
EXIDEIND.why: Exide has the strongest brand and balance sheet among battery makers but the lowest returns in this peer set (ROCE 9% vs 15-28% for Uno Minda, Bosch and HBL) because of the pre-revenue lithium-ion plant. Roughly level with Amara Raja, which faces the same transition. Fresh holding with a strong core quarter but an unproven capex cycle: HOLD.

best_own.name: Uno Minda
best_own.why: Diversified auto-component compounder with 20%-plus ROCE, consistent content-per-vehicle gains and EV-agnostic growth.

avoid.name: Eveready Industries India
avoid.why: Sub-scale consumer dry-cell business with a history of promoter pledge and leverage issues and weak returns.

BIRLACABLE.set: Indian telecom / optical fibre and cable manufacturers
BIRLACABLE.why: Birla Cable ranks last: smallest scale, weakest margins through the cycle, no investor communication, and a pending swap into Vindhya Telelinks that values it about 37% below the current price. The Q1 FY27 profit jump does not accrue to BCL holders on a standalone basis once the scheme is effective. Evidence is strong enough to move off the default HOLD to TRIM.

best_own.name: Finolex Cables
best_own.why: Net-cash, brand-led wires and cables franchise with double-digit margins and consistent returns, without corporate-action risk.

avoid.name: Sterlite Technologies
avoid.why: History of losses, high leverage and repeated restructuring make its earnings the least predictable in the set.

PENIND.set: Indian engineered-steel, PEB and tubes manufacturers
PENIND.why: Pennar offers more diversification than pure PEB peers but carries more debt and lower margins than Interarch (net cash) or Ratnamani (20%-plus ROCE). Consistent profit growth and a credible order book place it mid-table; leverage and the untested FY27 guidance keep it at HOLD.

best_own.name: Ratnamani Metals & Tubes
best_own.why: Best-in-class stainless and carbon steel tube franchise with net cash, 20%-plus ROCE and a long record of margin discipline.

avoid.name: Everest Industries
avoid.why: Steel-buildings segment losses and weak returns in recent years make it the least attractive in the set.

UNIPARTS.set: Indian precision components and forgings suppliers to global off-highway/auto OEMs
UNIPARTS.why: Uniparts has the best balance sheet and margins in this set (net cash, 24% EBITDA margin, 22% ROCE) but smaller scale and a narrower, more cyclical niche than Bharat Forge or Happy Forgings. Ranked third; fresh holding after a 113% one-year run, so HOLD rather than ADD.

best_own.name: Bharat Forge
best_own.why: Largest and most diversified forging franchise with defence and aerospace optionality and global OEM breadth.

avoid.name: Ramkrishna Forgings
avoid.why: Disclosed an inventory shortfall requiring restatement in 2025 and carries higher leverage than peers.

RISHABH.set: Indian electrical measurement, metering and automation equipment makers
RISHABH.why: Rishabh's core instruments business grows faster than most peers and carries no debt, but the group is held back by Alucast losses, small scale and an unresolved promoter-exit overhang; it sits mid-table below the MNC automation names and Genus's smart-meter order book. Fresh holding: HOLD pending clarity on control.

best_own.name: Honeywell Automation India
best_own.why: MNC parentage, high-margin building and process automation franchise, net cash and a long record of steady returns.

avoid.name: HPL Electric & Power
avoid.why: Leveraged, working-capital-heavy meter and switchgear maker with thin margins and volatile government-order dependence.

SUDEEPPHRM.set: Indian specialty pharma ingredients, excipients and nutraceutical API makers
SUDEEPPHRM.why: Sudeep's margins and ROCE are peer-leading and growth is faster than most, but scale, cash conversion and a nine-month listed record are well behind Divi's or Concord, and the multiple already discounts the greenfield ramp. Fresh holding with strong operating momentum but thin evidence: HOLD.

best_own.name: Divi's Laboratories
best_own.why: Scale leader in APIs and nutraceutical ingredients with net cash, 30%-plus margins and a decades-long regulatory compliance record.

avoid.name: Solara Active Pharma Sciences
avoid.why: Recent losses, restructuring and balance-sheet stress make it the weakest in the set.
